prompt: Users whose department attribute is "Sales" must be added to a group automatically. What should you create?

options.text: A Microsoft 365 group with Assigned membership
A security group with Dynamic User membership
A security group with Dynamic Device membership

explanation: Dynamic User membership evaluates a rule like user.department -eq "Sales" and adds or removes members on its own. It needs Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2. Assigned is manual, Dynamic Device targets devices, and administrative units scope admin permissions — they don't add members.

prompt: Which group type supports Dynamic Device membership?
explanation: Only security groups can hold devices, so only security groups support Dynamic Device rules. Microsoft 365 groups are collaboration groups (mailbox, Teams, SharePoint) and contain users only.

prompt: You try to assign a Microsoft 365 E3 license to User1 and the assignment fails. You are a License Administrator. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: User1 is not in a security group
User1 has no Usage location set

explanation: A license can't be assigned until the user's Usage location is set, because service availability depends on country. This is one of the most tested Entra licensing facts.

prompt: You want licenses assigned automatically to everyone added to the "Finance" group. What is the minimum requirement?

options.text: Microsoft Entra ID P1 (or a plan that includes it)

explanation: Group-based licensing requires Entra ID P1 or a suite that includes it (such as Microsoft 365 E3/E5 or Business Premium). P2 also works but isn't the minimum.

prompt: You need to create 300 new user accounts from a spreadsheet using the Entra admin center. What should you use?

options.text: Bulk create with the downloadable CSV template

explanation: Users > Bulk operations > Bulk create gives you a CSV template to fill and upload. Entra Connect syncs from on-premises AD, which isn't what's asked.

prompt: A user account was deleted 12 days ago. Can you restore it with its group memberships and licenses?

options.text: No, deleted users can't be restored
Yes, deleted users can be restored for 30 days
Only if the user was synced from on-premises

explanation: Deleted users stay in Deleted users for 30 days and restore with most properties. After 30 days they're permanently deleted.

prompt: A consultant from Fabrikam needs access to an Azure resource group using their own Fabrikam credentials. What should you do?

options.text: Create a new member account in your tenant
Invite them as a B2B guest user
Create a service principal for them
Add them to an administrative unit

explanation: B2B collaboration invites an external person as a Guest. They sign in with their own organization's identity, so you don't manage their password.

prompt: Only users assigned specific admin roles should be able to invite guests. Where do you configure this?
explanation: External Identities > External collaboration settings controls who can invite guests (everyone, members, admins and Guest Inviter role only, or no one).

prompt: You enable SSPR for "Selected" users. How many groups can you select?
explanation: With the Selected scope, SSPR targets a single group. To include more people, nest them in that group or switch to All.

prompt: SSPR requires 2 authentication methods. User1 has only registered a mobile phone. What happens when User1 tries to reset their password?

options.text: User1 can't reset until a second method is registered
User1 is automatically prompted for a security question instead
The policy is ignored for users with one method

explanation: When the policy requires two methods, the user must have two registered. With one, the reset is blocked.

prompt: You configure SSPR to require one method (email). A Global Administrator tries to reset their password with only email. What happens?

options.text: It works because the policy requires one method
It fails: administrators always use a stronger two-method policy
It works only from a compliant device

explanation: Admin accounts always get Microsoft's built-in admin SSPR policy, which requires two methods and doesn't allow security questions, regardless of your user policy.

prompt: Users are synced from on-premises Active Directory. Passwords changed through SSPR must update on-premises. What do you need?

options.text: Password writeback in Entra Connect or Cloud Sync (Entra ID P1)

explanation: Password writeback sends SSPR changes back to AD DS. It's configured in Entra Connect / Cloud Sync and requires Entra ID P1.

prompt: A help desk team in Pittsburgh should reset passwords only for users in the Pittsburgh office. What should you use?

options.text: An administrative unit with a scoped Helpdesk Administrator role

explanation: Administrative units let you scope Entra roles (like Helpdesk Administrator) to a subset of users or devices.

prompt: A user must create and manage all resources in RG1 but must NOT be able to grant access to others. Which role?
explanation: Contributor manages everything except role assignments. Owner can also assign roles. User Access Administrator manages access only.

prompt: A user must manage role assignments in a subscription but must not modify resources. Which built-in role follows least privilege?
explanation: Role Based Access Control Administrator (or User Access Administrator) manages access without resource management rights. Owner does both. Global Administrator is an Entra role, not Azure RBAC.

prompt: User1 has Reader on Subscription1 and Contributor on RG2 (inside Subscription1). What can User1 do to a VM in RG2?
explanation: Azure RBAC is additive: effective permissions are the union of all assignments at that scope and above. Contributor wins on RG2.

prompt: Where can you see every role assignment that gives a specific user access to a storage account?

options.text: Storage account > Access control (IAM) > Check access

explanation: Check access shows the user's effective assignments at that resource, including inherited ones.

prompt: Which statement about deny assignments is true?

options.text: Deny assignments block actions even when a role assignment allows them
You create deny assignments in the IAM blade like role assignments
Deny assignments only apply to guests

explanation: Deny assignments take precedence over role assignments. You don't create them directly; Azure creates them (for example, managed applications and deployment stacks).

prompt: Operators must start, stop and restart VMs but not create or delete them. No built-in role matches. What should you do?

options.text: Create a custom role with only the needed Actions
Assign Reader plus a resource lock

explanation: A custom role (JSON) lists the exact Actions — e.g. Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/start/action, restart/action, deallocate/action — plus AssignableScopes. VM Contributor would also allow create/delete.

prompt: A Global Administrator can't see any Azure subscriptions in the portal. What should they do first?

options.text: Assign themselves Owner from the subscription IAM blade
Turn on "Access management for Azure resources" in Entra ID properties

explanation: Entra roles and Azure RBAC are separate. The elevate-access toggle makes the Global Admin User Access Administrator at root scope (/) so they can grant themselves a role.

prompt: What is the difference between Azure RBAC and Azure Policy?

options.text: RBAC controls what resources look like; Policy controls who can act
RBAC controls who can act; Policy controls what can be created and how it's configured
Policy only applies to Entra users

explanation: RBAC = who can do what. Policy = rules on the resources themselves, regardless of who's acting.

prompt: Resources must only be created in East US and Central US. Which built-in policy and effect?
explanation: Allowed locations with the Deny effect blocks create/update requests outside the list.

prompt: You assign an Allowed locations (Deny) policy. VMs already exist in West US. What happens to them?

options.text: They are moved to an allowed region
They keep running and show as Non-compliant

explanation: Policy never deletes or moves existing resources with Deny. It marks them non-compliant and blocks new non-compliant creates or updates.

prompt: You want a report of resources without a CostCenter tag, without blocking deployments. Which effect?
explanation: Audit records non-compliance in the compliance view but lets the request through.

prompt: Every new resource must automatically receive Environment = Prod if the tag is missing. Which effect?
explanation: Modify adds, replaces or removes tags/properties during create or update. (Append is the older option for adding fields.)

prompt: Any VM without the Azure Monitor Agent should have it deployed automatically. Which effect?
explanation: DeployIfNotExists runs a template deployment when a related resource (here, the extension) is missing.

prompt: A Modify policy now tags new resources, but 200 existing resources are still missing the tag. What should you do?
explanation: Remediation tasks fix existing non-compliant resources. They only work with Modify and DeployIfNotExists, and the assignment needs a managed identity with the right permissions.

prompt: You need to assign 15 related policies for a compliance standard as one unit. What do you create?
explanation: An initiative groups policy definitions so you assign, track and report on them together.

prompt: A policy is assigned to Subscription1, but RG-Lab must not be evaluated. What do you configure?

options.text: An exclusion on the policy assignment

explanation: Assignments support exclusions for child scopes such as resource groups or resources.

prompt: A ReadOnly lock is applied to RG1, which contains VM1. A user with Owner tries to start VM1. What happens?

options.text: VM1 starts because Owner overrides locks
VM1 starts but can't be stopped

explanation: Starting a VM is a POST (write-type) operation. ReadOnly blocks it for everyone, including Owners, until the lock is removed.

prompt: A ReadOnly lock is on storage account st1. A Contributor opens Access keys in the portal. What happens?
explanation: Listing keys is a POST operation (listKeys), which ReadOnly blocks. A classic exam trap.

prompt: You must prevent accidental deletion of a production VNet while still allowing configuration changes. Which lock?
explanation: CanNotDelete allows reads and modifications but blocks deletion.

prompt: Which built-in roles can create or delete management locks?

options.text: Any user with access to the resource

explanation: Lock management requires Microsoft.Authorization/locks/* — granted to Owner and User Access Administrator (not Contributor).

prompt: RG1 is tagged Dept = IT. You create a VM in RG1. Which tags does the VM have?
explanation: Tags are not inherited. Use the built-in policy "Inherit a tag from the resource group" (Modify) to copy them down.

prompt: What is the maximum number of tag name/value pairs on one Azure resource?
explanation: Each resource, resource group or subscription supports up to 50 tags.

prompt: You need to move resources to a subscription in a different Microsoft Entra tenant. What must happen first?

options.text: Nothing, moves across tenants are supported
Transfer the target subscription into the same tenant
Export and re-import the Entra users

explanation: Resource moves only work between subscriptions in the same tenant.

prompt: During a resource move between resource groups, what is true?

options.text: Both resource groups are locked for create, update and delete until the move finishes
Only the destination group is locked

explanation: Both groups are locked during the move, but resources keep running. Resource IDs change because the RG is part of the ID.

prompt: A budget of $1,000/month is reached. What happens to running resources?

options.text: Nothing — budgets only alert, unless you attach an action group that triggers automation

explanation: Budgets send alerts. To act, attach an action group (for example, a runbook that shuts down VMs).

prompt: Where do you find recommendations to resize underused VMs and buy reservations?
explanation: Azure Advisor provides Cost, Security, Reliability, Operational Excellence and Performance recommendations.

prompt: How many levels deep can a management group hierarchy go, not counting the root and subscriptions?
explanation: Up to six levels of depth below the root group, excluding the subscription level.

prompt: How many parent management groups can a subscription have?
explanation: Each subscription and management group has exactly one parent.

prompt: You manage 12 subscriptions that need the same policies and RBAC. What is the best approach?

options.text: Place the subscriptions under one management group and assign there

explanation: Assignments on a management group are inherited by every subscription beneath it.

prompt: Which is the minimum license to create dynamic groups in Microsoft Entra ID?
explanation: Dynamic membership requires Entra ID P1 for each user who is a member of a dynamic group.

prompt: You must prevent users from registering applications in the tenant. Where do you configure this?
explanation: Entra ID > User settings controls whether users can register applications (and other default user permissions).

prompt: A cost alert should fire when daily spending deviates sharply from normal patterns. Which alert type?
explanation: Cost anomaly alerts use detection on daily spend to notify you about unusual changes.

prompt: Data must survive the loss of an entire Azure datacenter within the primary region, with no secondary region. Lowest-cost option?
explanation: ZRS keeps three copies across availability zones in one region, so it survives a datacenter (zone) failure. LRS keeps all copies in one datacenter. GRS adds a second region, which you don't need.

prompt: Data must survive a regional outage, and applications must be able to READ from the secondary region at any time. Which redundancy?
explanation: RA-GRS (or RA-GZRS) gives a readable secondary endpoint (accountname-secondary). Plain GRS only allows access to the secondary after a failover.

prompt: How many copies of data does GRS maintain in total?
explanation: Three copies in the primary region (LRS) plus three in the paired secondary region = six.

prompt: You need a premium file share for low-latency workloads. Which storage account kind?
explanation: Premium Azure Files requires a FileStorage (premium file shares) account. General-purpose v2 supports standard file shares only.

prompt: Which redundancy options are available for premium file shares?
explanation: Premium accounts support LRS and ZRS only (no geo-redundancy).

prompt: What are the naming rules for a storage account?

options.text: 3–24 characters, lowercase letters and numbers, globally unique
1–64 characters, hyphens allowed, unique per subscription
3–63 characters, any case, unique per region

explanation: Storage account names are 3–24 lowercase letters and numbers, and globally unique because they form the endpoint URL.

prompt: Blobs are rarely accessed and must be stored at the lowest cost. They can tolerate retrieval taking hours. Which tier?
explanation: Archive is the cheapest to store but offline: blobs must be rehydrated (up to 15 hours at Standard priority) before reading.

prompt: Can you set Archive as the default access tier of a storage account?

options.text: No — Archive can only be set on individual blobs

explanation: The account default tier can be Hot, Cool or Cold. Archive is set per blob (manually or by lifecycle rules).

prompt: A blob in Archive must be readable in under an hour. What do you do?

options.text: Change tier to Hot with High rehydrate priority

explanation: Rehydrate with High priority (typically under an hour for objects under 10 GB). Standard priority can take up to 15 hours.

prompt: Blobs should move to Cool after 30 days without modification, to Archive after 90 days, and be deleted after 365 days. What should you configure?
explanation: Lifecycle management rules tier or delete blobs based on age (last modified, created, or last accessed if access tracking is on). Policy runs about once a day.

prompt: A lifecycle rule must use "days since last accessed". What must you enable first?
explanation: daysAfterLastAccessTimeGreaterThan requires last access time tracking enabled on the account.

prompt: Which blob type is optimized for VHD disk files with random read/write?
explanation: Page blobs store random-access files such as VHDs. Block blobs hold general files; append blobs suit logs.

prompt: An external partner needs read access to one container for 7 days. You must NOT share account keys. Most secure SAS type if you can use Entra credentials?
explanation: A user delegation SAS is signed with Entra credentials instead of the account key, so it's the recommended and most secure SAS. It's for Blob storage (and Data Lake).

prompt: You issued several service SAS tokens for container1 without a stored access policy. You must revoke them immediately. What do you do?

options.text: Delete the SAS from the portal
Regenerate the account key used to sign them
Change the container's access level to private

explanation: A SAS without a policy can only be revoked by rotating the key that signed it (or waiting for expiry). That's why stored access policies are recommended.

prompt: How do stored access policies help with SAS management?

options.text: They let you change or revoke a group of service SAS tokens by editing or deleting the policy
They extend SAS lifetime beyond 7 days

explanation: A service SAS can reference a stored access policy on the container. Changing the policy's expiry or deleting it revokes every SAS linked to it.

prompt: How many stored access policies can a single blob container have?
explanation: Up to five stored access policies per container, file share, queue or table.

prompt: Why does a storage account have two access keys?

options.text: One for read, one for write
So you can rotate one key while apps use the other
One for SAS, one for SMB

explanation: Rotate key2, switch apps to it, then rotate key1 — no downtime. Better still, store keys in Key Vault or use Entra auth.

prompt: You want to force all clients to use Entra ID or SAS signed by Entra and block account-key access. What do you set?

options.text: Allow storage account key access = Disabled

explanation: Disabling Shared Key authorization blocks requests signed with account keys (including account/service SAS).

prompt: Storage account st1 must accept traffic only from Subnet1 in VNet1, without giving st1 a private IP. What do you configure?

options.text: A service endpoint for Microsoft.Storage on Subnet1 and a VNet rule on the st1 firewall

explanation: Service endpoints let the subnet's traffic reach the storage public endpoint over the Azure backbone with the VNet identity. Then the firewall allows that subnet. A private endpoint would give st1 a private IP.

prompt: You add your office public IP 10.0.0.25 to a storage firewall IP rule. Why does it fail?

options.text: IP rules accept only private ranges
IP rules don't accept private (RFC 1918) addresses

explanation: Storage IP network rules apply to public IPs only. Private addresses must use VNet rules or private endpoints.

prompt: Azure Backup must access a storage account that has firewall rules enabled. What do you allow?

options.text: "Allow Azure services on the trusted services list to access this storage account"
A public IP rule for Azure Backup

explanation: The trusted services exception allows specific Microsoft services (such as Azure Backup) through the firewall.

prompt: Users on-premises can't mount an Azure file share over SMB, but it works inside Azure. Most likely cause?

options.text: Port 445 outbound is blocked by the ISP or firewall
The share is on Hot tier

explanation: SMB uses TCP 445, which many ISPs and corporate firewalls block. Use VPN/ExpressRoute or Azure File Sync.

prompt: Hybrid users (synced from AD DS) must access Azure Files with their identities from Entra-joined devices without line of sight to domain controllers. Which identity source?
explanation: Microsoft Entra Kerberos lets Entra-joined clients get Kerberos tickets for Azure Files for hybrid identities.

prompt: In Azure File Sync, how many cloud endpoints can a sync group contain?
explanation: A sync group has exactly one cloud endpoint (an Azure file share) and one or more server endpoints.

prompt: A file server has limited disk space. Frequently used files must stay local, and cold files should live only in Azure. Which Azure File Sync feature?
explanation: Cloud tiering keeps hot files local and replaces cold files with pointers that recall on access.

prompt: Deleted blobs must be recoverable for 14 days. What do you enable?
explanation: Blob soft delete keeps deleted blobs (and overwritten snapshots) for 1–365 days.

prompt: Someone deleted an entire container. Which feature would let you restore it?
explanation: Container soft delete protects against deleting the container itself; blob soft delete protects blobs inside existing containers.

prompt: Each overwrite of a blob must automatically keep the previous version. What do you enable?
explanation: Versioning automatically saves the previous state on every write. Snapshots are manual point-in-time copies.

prompt: You need a read-only, point-in-time copy of an Azure file share before an upgrade. What do you create?
explanation: Share snapshots capture the share at a point in time and can be used to restore files.

prompt: Which command copies a local folder and all subfolders to a blob container with AzCopy?
explanation: azcopy copy <source> <destination> --recursive. Authenticate with a SAS on the URL or azcopy login (Entra ID).

prompt: Which AzCopy command makes a destination match the source, copying only changed files?
explanation: azcopy sync compares source and destination by last-modified time and copies only what changed (optionally deleting extras).

prompt: Storage data must be encrypted with keys your company controls and can rotate. What do you configure?

options.text: Customer-managed keys in Azure Key Vault

explanation: Customer-managed keys live in Key Vault or Managed HSM. The vault needs soft delete and purge protection, and the storage account uses a managed identity to reach the key.

prompt: When can you enable infrastructure encryption (double encryption) on a storage account?
explanation: Infrastructure encryption must be enabled at account creation; it can't be turned on later.

prompt: Is Azure Storage data encrypted at rest by default?
explanation: Storage service encryption is always on and can't be disabled. You choose Microsoft-managed or customer-managed keys.

prompt: Records must be stored in a write-once, read-many state for 7 years for compliance. What do you use?

options.text: Immutable storage with a time-based retention policy

explanation: Immutable blob storage (WORM) supports time-based retention and legal holds. Even admins can't delete or modify during retention.

prompt: Which tool gives a GUI to browse blobs, manage SAS and upload files across accounts from your desktop?
explanation: Storage Explorer is the desktop GUI (it uses AzCopy under the hood for transfers).

prompt: You need to transfer 80 TB to Azure, and the internet link would take months. What should you use?
explanation: Azure Data Box ships physical devices for offline bulk transfer.

prompt: Which policy effects support remediation tasks? (Select TWO.)
explanation: Only Modify and DeployIfNotExists can change existing resources through remediation, using the assignment's managed identity.

prompt: You configure object replication from st1 to st2. Which features must be enabled? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Change feed on the source account

explanation: Object replication requires versioning on source and destination, and change feed on the source. Hierarchical namespace isn't supported.

prompt: You redeploy an ARM template to RG1 in Complete mode. RG1 contains a storage account that isn't in the template. What happens?

options.text: It's moved to a new RG

explanation: Complete mode makes the RG match the template exactly, deleting resources not defined in it. Incremental (the default) leaves them alone.

prompt: What is the default ARM deployment mode?
explanation: Incremental is the default: it adds or updates resources in the template and leaves others untouched.

prompt: You must deploy the same template to dev, test and prod with different VM sizes, without editing the template. What should you use?

options.text: A separate parameters file per environment

explanation: Parameters accept values at deployment time; a parameters file per environment keeps the template the same.

prompt: A storage account name in a template must be globally unique and repeatable for the same resource group. Which expression?
explanation: uniqueString() returns a deterministic 13-character hash, so the same RG always produces the same name. newGuid() changes every deployment.

prompt: A VM in a template must be created only after its NIC exists. What do you add to the VM resource?
explanation: dependsOn sets deployment order. (Bicep usually infers dependencies from symbolic references.)

prompt: You have an existing ARM template and want to convert it to Bicep. Which command?
explanation: decompile converts ARM JSON to Bicep. build compiles Bicep to ARM JSON.

prompt: You configured resources in the portal and want a reusable template of RG1. What do you do?

options.text: Export template from the resource group

explanation: Resource group > Export template (or from a deployment's history) generates a template you can edit and redeploy.

prompt: Which Azure CLI command deploys a Bicep file to a resource group?

options.text: az deployment group create --resource-group RG1 --template-file main.bicep

explanation: az deployment group create (CLI) or New-AzResourceGroupDeployment (PowerShell). Use az deployment sub create for subscription-scope deployments.

prompt: You need 99.99% VM availability SLA within a region. What should you deploy?

options.text: Two VMs in an availability set
Two or more VMs across availability zones
One VM with a load balancer

explanation: Two or more VMs across availability zones = 99.99%. Availability set = 99.95%. Single VM with Premium SSD = 99.9%.

prompt: What do update domains in an availability set protect against?

options.text: Planned maintenance rebooting all VMs at once

explanation: Update domains are rebooted one at a time during planned maintenance. Fault domains separate power and network hardware (rack failures).

prompt: What are the maximum fault domains and update domains in an availability set?
explanation: Up to 3 fault domains (region dependent) and up to 20 update domains (default 5).

prompt: VM1 is already running. You want to add it to availability set AS1. What must you do?

options.text: Add it from the VM's Availability blade

explanation: A VM's availability set is set at creation. To change it, delete the VM (keep disks) and recreate it in the set.

prompt: You resize VM1 but the new size isn't listed. What should you try?
explanation: Sizes not available on the current hardware cluster appear after deallocation, because the VM can move to different hardware.

prompt: Which disk type can't be used as an OS disk?
explanation: Ultra Disks (and Premium SSD v2) are data disks only.

prompt: You need to increase a data disk from 128 GiB to 256 GiB. Can you later shrink it back?

options.text: No, managed disks can't be shrunk
Only when the VM is deallocated

explanation: You can expand managed disks, but you can't reduce their size.

prompt: Data on the VM's temp disk and disk caches must be encrypted at rest, end to end, without using BitLocker in the guest. What do you enable?
explanation: Encryption at host encrypts temp disks and caches on the host. It must be registered on the subscription (EncryptionAtHost feature) before enabling on the VM.

prompt: You use Azure Disk Encryption on a Windows VM. Where are the encryption keys stored?

options.text: In Azure Key Vault (enabled for disk encryption)

explanation: ADE uses BitLocker (Windows) or DM-Crypt (Linux) with keys/secrets in Key Vault, which must be enabled for Azure Disk Encryption and in the same region.

prompt: You need to move VM1 from East US to West US. What should you use?

options.text: Azure Resource Mover (or Azure Site Recovery)

explanation: Cross-region moves use Azure Resource Mover (which uses Site Recovery for VMs). Moving between RGs or subscriptions doesn't change region.

prompt: You move VM1 to another resource group. Which dependent resources should you move with it?

options.text: Its NIC, disks and (if needed) public IP

explanation: Move the VM with its dependent resources (disks, NIC, public IP). The portal validates dependencies before the move.

prompt: After deployment, a script must install IIS on 50 new Windows VMs. What should you use?
explanation: The Custom Script Extension downloads and runs scripts on VMs after deployment.

prompt: A web tier must add VMs automatically when average CPU is above 75% and remove them below 25%. What do you deploy?

options.text: Virtual Machine Scale Set with autoscale rules

explanation: Scale sets support autoscale rules on metrics (scale out / scale in) with minimum, maximum and default instance counts.

prompt: A scale set has min 2, max 10, default 2. A scale-out rule adds 1 instance when CPU > 75%. CPU stays at 90% all day. How many instances at most?
explanation: Autoscale never goes above the maximum instance count (10).

prompt: Which scale set upgrade policy applies model changes to instances only when you manually upgrade them?
explanation: Manual: you choose when to update instances. Automatic upgrades all immediately; Rolling upgrades in batches.

prompt: You need a private container registry with geo-replication to two regions. Minimum ACR tier?
explanation: Geo-replication (and private endpoints) require ACR Premium.

prompt: You need to build a container image in Azure from a Dockerfile without Docker installed locally. Which command?
explanation: az acr build runs an ACR Task that builds and pushes the image in the cloud.

prompt: You need to run a container for a short batch job with per-second billing and no orchestration. Simplest service?
explanation: ACI runs containers on demand, billed per second, with no cluster to manage.

prompt: An ACI container runs a nightly job. It must restart if it crashes, but must not restart after it completes successfully. Which restart policy?
explanation: OnFailure restarts only if the container exits with an error. Never doesn't restart at all; Always restarts even after success.

prompt: Two containers must share a lifecycle, local network and storage on the same host in ACI. What do you deploy?
explanation: A container group schedules containers together on one host, sharing lifecycle, network (localhost) and volumes. Multi-container groups use YAML or ARM.

prompt: A containerized API must scale on HTTP traffic and scale to zero when idle, without managing Kubernetes. Which service?
explanation: Container Apps is serverless with scale rules (HTTP, KEDA events) and scale to zero.

prompt: What is the lowest App Service plan tier that supports deployment slots and autoscale?
explanation: Standard (S1) and above support deployment slots and autoscale. Basic supports manual scale-out only.

prompt: You must test a new release in production conditions, then switch it live with no downtime and easy rollback. What do you use?
explanation: Deploy to a staging slot, warm it, then swap. Swapping back is the rollback.

prompt: A connection string must stay with the production slot and NOT move during a swap. What do you configure?

options.text: Mark it as a deployment slot setting (sticky)

explanation: Deployment slot settings ("sticky") stay with the slot during swaps.

prompt: You scale an App Service plan from S1 to P1v3. Is this scale up or scale out?
explanation: Scale up = bigger tier/hardware. Scale out = more instances.

prompt: You map www.contoso.com to an App Service app. Which DNS records are used for verification and mapping?

options.text: CNAME to the app's azurewebsites.net name plus a TXT asuid record

explanation: For a subdomain, create a CNAME to <app>.azurewebsites.net and a TXT asuid.www record for domain verification. A root domain uses an A record plus TXT asuid.

prompt: An App Service app must reach a database in a VNet (outbound). What do you configure?
explanation: VNet integration handles outbound traffic from the app into the VNet. Private endpoints handle inbound traffic to the app.

prompt: Which VM pricing option gives deep discounts but can be evicted when Azure needs capacity?
explanation: Spot VMs use spare capacity at a discount but can be evicted with 30 seconds notice.

prompt: A VM won't boot and you can't RDP or SSH. Which feature gives text-based access to the VM's console?
explanation: Serial console needs boot diagnostics enabled and works even when networking is broken.

prompt: Subnet1 is 10.0.1.0/24. How many IP addresses can you assign to resources?
explanation: Azure reserves 5 addresses per subnet: network (.0), gateway (.1), two for Azure DNS (.2, .3) and broadcast (.255). 256 − 5 = 251.

prompt: What is the first usable IP address in subnet 10.0.1.0/24?
explanation: The first four (.0–.3) are reserved, so .4 is the first assignable address.

prompt: VNet1 (10.0.0.0/16) and VNet2 (10.0.0.0/16) must be peered. What happens?

options.text: Peering fails because address spaces overlap

explanation: Peered VNets can't have overlapping address spaces.

prompt: VNet1 is peered with VNet2, and VNet2 is peered with VNet3. Can VMs in VNet1 reach VNet3?
explanation: Peering isn't transitive. Peer VNet1↔VNet3 directly, or route through an NVA/firewall or gateway in the hub with UDRs.

prompt: You create a peering from VNet1 to VNet2 only. What is the peering status?
explanation: A peering shows Initiated until the reverse link (VNet2 → VNet1) is created; then both become Connected. The portal can create both at once.

prompt: Spoke VNets must use the VPN gateway in the hub VNet to reach on-premises. Which peering settings?

options.text: Allow gateway transit on the hub; Use remote gateways on the spokes
Use remote gateways on the hub; Allow gateway transit on the spokes

explanation: The hub (with the gateway) allows gateway transit; each spoke uses the remote gateway.

prompt: Can you peer VNets in different Azure regions?
explanation: Global VNet peering connects VNets across regions over the Microsoft backbone.

prompt: All internet-bound traffic from Subnet1 must go through a firewall VM at 10.0.0.4. What do you create?

options.text: Route table with 0.0.0.0/0 next hop Virtual appliance 10.0.0.4, associated with Subnet1

explanation: A user-defined route overrides the system default route. Also enable IP forwarding on the firewall VM's NIC.

prompt: Two routes match a destination: 10.0.0.0/16 (system) and 10.0.1.0/24 (user-defined). Which is used for 10.0.1.5?
explanation: Azure picks the most specific prefix first. For equal prefixes: UDR > BGP > system.

prompt: A VM is configured as a router (NVA). Packets not addressed to it are dropped. What must you enable in Azure?
explanation: Azure drops traffic not destined for a NIC's own IP unless IP forwarding is enabled on that NIC (and in the guest OS).

prompt: NSG1 has inbound rules: priority 100 Deny TCP 3389 from Any, priority 200 Allow TCP 3389 from 203.0.113.5. Can 203.0.113.5 connect over RDP?
explanation: Rules are processed from lowest number up and stop at the first match. Priority 100 denies first.

prompt: What is the valid priority range for custom NSG rules?
explanation: Custom rules use 100–4096. Default rules use 65000–65500 and can't be deleted (only overridden).

prompt: An NSG on Subnet1 allows RDP, and an NSG on VM1's NIC denies RDP. Can you RDP to VM1?
explanation: Both NSGs are evaluated. Inbound traffic must be allowed by the subnet NSG and then the NIC NSG.

prompt: NSGs are stateful. What does that mean?

options.text: You must create matching outbound rules for replies
Return traffic for an allowed connection is allowed automatically

explanation: If inbound is allowed, the response is allowed out automatically (and vice versa).

prompt: Web VMs and DB VMs share a subnet. Only web VMs may reach DB VMs on 1433, without managing IP addresses. What do you use?

options.text: Application security groups referenced in NSG rules

explanation: ASGs group NICs by role (ASG-Web, ASG-DB); the NSG rule allows ASG-Web → ASG-DB on 1433.

prompt: Which statement about application security groups is true?

options.text: NICs in an ASG can be in any VNet
All NICs in an ASG must be in the same VNet

explanation: NICs in an ASG must belong to the same VNet as the first NIC added.

prompt: Which Network Watcher tool tells you which NSG rule allowed or denied a specific packet to a VM?
explanation: IP flow verify tests a 5-tuple and returns allow/deny plus the rule name.

prompt: A VM can't reach the internet, and you suspect a UDR. Which Network Watcher tool shows the route used?
explanation: Next hop shows the next hop type and route table used for a destination.

prompt: Where do you see the combined NSG rules applied to a NIC from both subnet and NIC NSGs?
explanation: Effective security rules shows the aggregate rules on a NIC.

prompt: Admins must RDP/SSH to VMs from the portal over TLS without public IPs on the VMs. What do you deploy?
explanation: Azure Bastion provides RDP/SSH over 443 in the browser; VMs need no public IP.

prompt: What subnet requirements does Azure Bastion have?
explanation: Bastion must be in a subnet named AzureBastionSubnet, at least /26.

prompt: Admins want to connect with their native SSH/RDP client through Bastion. Minimum SKU?
explanation: Native client support, IP-based connection and shareable links need Standard or Premium.

prompt: A storage account must be reachable from the VNet through a private IP, and public access will be disabled. What do you create?
explanation: A private endpoint is a NIC with a private IP in your subnet mapped to the service. Pair it with a private DNS zone (privatelink.blob.core.windows.net).

prompt: After creating a private endpoint for st1 blob, VMs still resolve st1 to its public IP. What's missing?

options.text: Private DNS zone privatelink.blob.core.windows.net linked to the VNet

explanation: Private endpoints rely on DNS. The privatelink zone with an A record, linked to the VNet, makes the name resolve to the private IP.

prompt: You bought contoso.com from a registrar and created a public DNS zone in Azure DNS. What makes Azure DNS authoritative?

options.text: Update the NS records at the registrar to Azure DNS name servers
Link the zone to a VNet

explanation: Delegation: point the domain's NS records at the registrar to the four Azure DNS name servers shown on the zone.

prompt: VMs in VNet1 must automatically register their hostnames in contoso.internal. What do you configure?

options.text: Private DNS zone linked to VNet1 with autoregistration enabled
Custom DNS server on each VM

explanation: A private DNS zone virtual network link with autoregistration creates records for VMs automatically. A VNet can have autoregistration with only one private zone.

prompt: You want contoso.com (apex) to point to an Azure public IP and update automatically if the IP changes. Which record?
explanation: CNAMEs can't be used at the zone apex. Alias records point to Azure resources and follow IP changes.

prompt: What IP do Azure VMs use by default for Azure-provided DNS?
explanation: 168.63.129.16 is Azure's virtual IP for DNS and health probes. 169.254.169.254 is the instance metadata service.

prompt: Load balancer backend VMs are healthy, but the probe shows them all down. NSGs allow port 80 from Internet only. What's wrong?

options.text: The probe needs the AzureLoadBalancer service tag allowed

explanation: Health probes come from 168.63.129.16 (the AzureLoadBalancer tag). Default NSG rules allow it, but a custom deny can block it.

prompt: You need to load balance traffic from web VMs to app VMs inside a VNet, with no public exposure. What do you deploy?
explanation: An internal load balancer uses a private frontend IP.

prompt: Users need URL path-based routing (/images to pool A, /api to pool B) and a web application firewall. What do you use?
explanation: Application Gateway is a layer 7 load balancer with path-based routing, TLS termination and WAF. Load Balancer is layer 4.

prompt: RDP must reach individual backend VMs through the load balancer's public IP on different ports (50001 → VM1:3389). What do you configure?
explanation: Inbound NAT rules forward a frontend port to a specific backend instance and port.

prompt: A user's sessions must stick to the same backend VM on a load balancer. What do you set?
explanation: Session persistence (source IP affinity) sends a client to the same backend.

prompt: Which statement about Standard public IP addresses is true?

options.text: They're open to the internet by default
They're secure by default and need an NSG to allow inbound traffic

explanation: Standard SKU public IPs are static, can be zone-redundant, and are closed to inbound traffic until an NSG allows it. (Basic SKU was retired in 2025.)

prompt: What must the subnet for a VPN gateway be named?
explanation: It must be named GatewaySubnet. /27 or larger is recommended.

prompt: VMs without public IPs need outbound internet access through a fixed set of public IPs. Best service?
explanation: A NAT gateway provides scalable outbound SNAT for a subnet using static public IPs.

prompt: You need to continuously test reachability and latency from a VM to an on-premises server and alert when it fails. Which tool?
explanation: Connection Monitor continuously checks connectivity and latency between endpoints and integrates with alerts.

prompt: VM guest performance counters and Windows event logs must go to a Log Analytics workspace. What do you need?

options.text: Azure Monitor Agent with a data collection rule

explanation: Guest OS data is collected by the Azure Monitor Agent; the data collection rule says what to collect and where to send it.

prompt: Platform logs from a storage account (read/write requests) must go to Log Analytics. What do you configure?
explanation: Resource logs are routed with diagnostic settings to Log Analytics, a storage account, or Event Hubs.

prompt: Who deleted a VM yesterday? Where do you look first?
explanation: The activity log records subscription control-plane operations (who, what, when), kept for 90 days.

prompt: How long does the activity log keep data by default?
explanation: 90 days. Send it to Log Analytics or storage with a diagnostic setting to keep it longer.

prompt: Which KQL operator selects only specific columns?
explanation: project chooses columns; extend adds calculated columns; where filters rows.

prompt: An alert must email the on-call team, send an SMS, and start a runbook. Where do you define those notifications and actions?
explanation: Action groups hold notifications (email, SMS, push, voice) and actions (runbook, Logic App, webhook, Function, ITSM). Many alert rules can share one.

prompt: During a planned maintenance window every Saturday 2–4 AM, alert notifications must be suppressed without disabling alert rules. What do you use?
explanation: Alert processing rules can suppress notifications on a schedule, or add action groups to many alerts at scale.

prompt: What does alert severity Sev 0 mean?
explanation: Sev 0 Critical, Sev 1 Error, Sev 2 Warning, Sev 3 Informational, Sev 4 Verbose.

prompt: You need dependency maps and performance charts across many VMs. What do you enable?
explanation: VM insights uses the Azure Monitor Agent (and a DCR) to show performance and, optionally, process dependency maps.

prompt: You need to back up Azure VMs. Which vault?
explanation: Azure VMs, SQL in VMs, Azure Files and MARS use Recovery Services vaults. Backup vaults handle newer workloads such as Azure Disks, Blobs and PostgreSQL.

prompt: VM1 is in East US. Where must the Recovery Services vault that backs it up be?

options.text: East US (same region as the VM)

explanation: For Azure VM backup, the vault must be in the same region as the VM.

prompt: You want to change a Recovery Services vault from GRS to LRS. When can you do it?

options.text: Only before any items are protected
Only after deleting backups older than 30 days

explanation: Storage replication type must be set before configuring backups for the first item.

prompt: A user deleted one file from a VM yesterday. Fastest way to get it back from Azure Backup?

options.text: File Recovery (mount the recovery point with a script)

explanation: File Recovery mounts the recovery point as a drive via a downloaded script so you copy single files.

prompt: Someone deletes backup data for a VM. How long can it be recovered by default?
explanation: Soft delete keeps deleted backup data for 14 days by default at no extra cost.

prompt: Backups must be restorable in the paired region even when the primary region is healthy. What do you enable?

options.text: Cross Region Restore (on a GRS vault)

explanation: Cross Region Restore requires a GRS vault and lets you restore in the secondary region at any time.

prompt: You need to back up files and folders on an on-premises Windows server directly to Azure. What do you install?
explanation: The Microsoft Azure Recovery Services (MARS) agent backs up files, folders and system state to a Recovery Services vault.

prompt: VMs in East US must fail over to West US during a regional outage, with minutes of data loss. What do you use?
explanation: Site Recovery continuously replicates VMs to another region for disaster recovery failover.

prompt: For Site Recovery from East US to West US, where should the Recovery Services vault be?
explanation: For Azure-to-Azure DR, the vault goes in the target (recovery) region, not the source.

prompt: You must prove your DR plan works without affecting production. What do you run?

options.text: Test failover into an isolated VNet

explanation: Test failover creates VMs in an isolated network; production replication continues. Clean up afterward.

prompt: Several VMs must fail over in order: database, then app, then web, with scripts in between. What do you create?
explanation: Recovery plans group machines, set failover order and run scripts or manual actions between groups.

prompt: You want Backup reports across vaults. What must be configured first?

options.text: Diagnostic settings sending vault data to a Log Analytics workspace

explanation: Backup reports are built on Log Analytics data from vault diagnostic settings.

prompt: Which Network Watcher feature records which IPs and ports flowed through a VNet for traffic analytics?
explanation: Flow logs (VNet flow logs replace NSG flow logs) record traffic and feed Traffic Analytics.

prompt: Which restore options are available for an Azure VM backup? (Select THREE.)

options.text: Restore to an on-premises Hyper-V host

explanation: VM restore can create a new VM, restore disks (then build a VM yourself), or replace the existing VM's disks.
